title: AlphaFold-Multimer predicted that Tmem81 joins a sperm complex, and experiments showed that zebrafish and mice need it for male fertility
summary: An AlphaFold-Multimer screen predicted that Tmem81 joins a sperm complex with Izumo1 and Spaca6; the Pauli laboratory then showed that Tmem81 is essential for male fertility in zebrafish and mice.
account: The Pauli laboratory and collaborators ran an AlphaFold-Multimer screen. It identified Tmem81 as part of a conserved trimeric sperm complex with the known essential fertilization factors Izumo1 and Spaca6. The prediction was then tested at the bench. The screen and the validation were performed independently of AlphaFold's developer. The Pauli laboratory first posted the result as a preprint on 28 July 2023. A separate team led by Arne Elofsson and Luca Jovine in Sweden used AlphaFold-Multimer to predict the same TMEM81 complex for the mammalian proteins. They posted their preprint on the same day and published the study in eLife on 26 April 2024. The Pauli laboratory published its paper in Cell on 17 October 2024. The authors demonstrated that Tmem81 is essential for male fertility in zebrafish and mice. They showed that Izumo1, Spaca6 and Tmem81 interact in zebrafish sperm and that the human orthologues interact in vitro. They found that complex formation creates the binding site for the egg factor Bouncer in zebrafish. In a preprint of 15 May 2026, the Pauli laboratory reports that the trimer belongs to a larger sperm complex, SPARK, whose parts are each required for male fertility in zebrafish and mice.
purpose: The laboratory used AlphaFold-Multimer to predict protein complexes and so to find missing parts of the machinery by which vertebrate sperm and egg interact.
deployer: Research Institute of Molecular Pathology (Pauli lab) and collaborators

ratings.reason: The screen predicted a specific candidate, Tmem81, that the laboratory then validated genetically and biochemically. This was a measurable research result for that group.

The laboratory identified a fertilization factor that vertebrates share and that male zebrafish and mice need to be fertile. This advances a long-standing open question. No source reports a clinical application.

ai_role.statement: AlphaFold-Multimer generated the hypothesis that Tmem81 belongs to a trimeric complex with Izumo1 and Spaca6. The functional claim rests on the same laboratory's wet-lab work: zebrafish and mouse knockouts, zebrafish sperm interaction assays, and human orthologue interaction in vitro.

evidence.citation: Elofsson A, Han L, Bianchi E, Wright GJ, Jovine L, Deep learning insights into the architecture of the mammalian egg-sperm fusion synapse, eLife 13:RP93131, 26 April 2024. The authors work at Stockholm University, Karolinska Institutet and the University of York, outside the Pauli group and DeepMind, with Swedish and British public funding. With AlphaFold-Multimer they predicted that TMEM81 joins IZUMO1, SPACA6 and the egg proteins JUNO and CD9 in a pentameric complex, and they did not test fertility in animals.
